messages:
Kai: Heads-up — we're scheduling a rolling drain/reboot for eu-west3 tonight due to tightening thermal margins across two racks. Window: 02:00-04:00 UTC. Expect ~10% capacity impact on hosted pools for ~45m while each rack cools down. Asking for quick sanity checks on Dedicated failovers and any high-latency tenants.

Sasha: tagging @Kai please confirm which pools are affected (hosted vs dedicated). Any regional fallback routing enabled?

Kai: Affected: hosted-gpu-pool-euw3-primary and hotbackfill pool euw3-saturn-1. Dedicated customers pinned to specific racks won't be touched unless they opt into failover. Smart routing will prefer eu-west1/eu-central for new requests.

Emmie: Do we have KV-cache prewarm notes? Cold KV will spike token latency. Recommend seeding after each node comes back: 
```
/opt/redwood/bin/kvseed --model all --region eu-west3 --parallel 8
```
We should run this as part of the node uncordon hook.

Liam: Cost heads-up: if traffic shifts to other regions we'll burn cross-region egress and burst capacity. Quick estimate: 2 hours of overflow -> ~€1.2k egress + extra GPU minutes. Ops budget aware?

Marcel: Ops budget is OK but want to keep burst <30m if possible. Plan: stagger rack drains 30m apart, cordon -> drain -> reboot -> wait thermal-stable -> uncordon. Sequence: rack-A -> rack-B. I'll post the exact node list in a sec.

Kai: Good. Also enabling fallback policy to route to smaller quantized variants for latency-sensitive routes during the drain (model-quant-128). That keeps tail latency low.

Sasha: Any customer-facing comms? We should notify support and CS for the small SLA blip window.

Emmie: I'll add a short note to the status page draft: "Planned maintenance in eu-west3, some request latency and throttling possible between 02:00-04:00 UTC. No expected data access issues." Liam/CS to approve.

Liam: Approved. Add a reminder to cancel background batch jobs hitting eu-west3 during the window — they cause noisy neighbor effects.

Marcel: Node list (partial): rack-A: node-euw3-a01..a10; rack-B: node-euw3-b01..b08. Drain command we will run via runbook agent: 
```
opsctl runbook execute thermal-drain --rack A --timeout 1800
```
Workflows have automated rollback if pressure doesn't drop within 20m.

Kai: Ops-bot will create a calendar event and page oncall at T-30. Please ack once you see the page.

ops-bot: Calendar event created: "eu-west3 thermal margin rolling drain" 2025-04-09 02:00-04:00 UTC. Paging oncall at 01:30 UTC.

Sasha: Acked. I'll brief support and pin the status draft. :thumbsup:

Emmie: I'll add the KV seed step to the uncordon hook and include a short wait-for-kv-health check.

Liam: One more ask — capture per-tenant latency + token-cost delta in the rollout so we can quantify cost vs benefit. If any tenant sees >20% tail latency, roll back routing to quant-64 variant.

Marcel: Noted. We'll collect traces and emit a rollout report to #eng-telemetry once complete.

Kai: Thanks all. If no objections I'll start the preflight run at 23:30 UTC (checks: capacity headroom, backups, backfill thresholds). If you see anything odd ping here or @oncall.

Sasha: No objections from me.

Emmie: All good.

Liam: Good to go.

Marcel: Ready on my side.

ops-bot: Oncall page sent to PagerDuty: eu-west3-team at 01:30 UTC. Event ID: PD-34812.
